analysis: Examined three changes. (1) NemotronSuperLocalOutput.swift head lines 93-98: response-format normalization is now skipped when the turn has validated tool calls, and the text passes through unchanged. Tool calls still go through ToolConstraintValidation.validate (line 92) and forced tool_choice still yields empty text. Malformed-frame handling, the byte bound (line 55) and the fail-closed paths are unchanged. The effect is that a turn with a tool call plus JSON-format content is no longer checked against the JSON contract. This is an output-contract relaxation for an adversarial provider's own output. It exposes no new confidentiality, authorization or billing path, and I found no regression against T-007 or T-008. (2) NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP.swift head lines 178-179: a new `.bodyTooLarge` case maps to MediaIngest.MediaError.mediaTooLarge with a fixed string that carries no prompt or media content. This keeps the 'no foreign descriptions' property of SuperHTTPErrors. The switch stays exhaustive only if NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding.Failure declares `.bodyTooLarge`; that file was not in the supplied batch. (3) The test change shows encodedHeaderQuote now accepts bodies up to NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes, with quote = bytes*32 + 4 + 16 MiB. It returns bodyTooLarge above that limit, and invalidInput for 0 bytes or oversized templates. The production encodedHeaderQuote implementation and the value of maximumEncodedBodyBytes are not visible. The next pass should check that the maximum was not raised above the old 8 MiB in a way that enlarges the pre-parse memory reservation, and that the 413 path is rejected before body parsing or media reservation. The mapping of mediaTooLarge to a 413 status in the HTTP layer is also unverified. No finding is raised because the required evidence is outside the supplied units.
